text: Designing a good REST API is like building a clear road map for developers. Start by defining logical endpoints, such as `/users` or `/orders`, where each endpoint represents a resource or action. Always use standard HTTP status codes—like 200 for success, 404 for not found, and 500 for server errors—so clients instantly understand the result. Write thorough documentation with examples and explanations; this saves hours of confusion later. Also, version your API from the beginning (for instance, `/v1/users`) to allow changes without breaking existing users. A well-planned API feels intuitive, reduces bugs, and makes integration smooth for everyone. Keep it simple, consistent, and thoughtfully documented.
